globalClauses.text: Supported platforms and capability matrix — Windows, 9to1-OS, web and other supported surfaces, including exact differences rather than silent feature loss.

Completion evidence MUST cover representative end-to-end journeys, persistence/restart behaviour, API/UI parity, permissions, accessibility, failure/recovery paths, donor parity where applicable and platform/package validation for every declared supported platform.

Web CUI MAY use a browser-specific implementation/runtime, but it MUST preserve the same public CUI semantics, component contracts, state identities and supported action/property behaviour except for explicitly declared platform capability differences.

Every installable/native 9to1 app has a hard runtime dependency on 9-1 Home. Before initialising the app’s normal UI or opening user artifacts, the app MUST complete a local Home availability/version handshake against the Home-managed shared services it requires.

This local-install dependency applies to native/installable clients. Browser-hosted web surfaces cannot require a local Home installation; they instead use the corresponding authenticated 9to1 shared web services and capability negotiation defined for web clients.

Cakemods.com MUST host a web version of every 9-1 Workspace/AI product that is not explicitly listed as web-exempt. Web surfaces MUST share the same CAKE ID identity, canonical artifact formats, domain APIs, permission model and underlying server-side entities as desktop equivalents. Browser-specific UI/layout MAY differ, but it MUST NOT create a separate incompatible product model.

The default rule is to provide a web version whenever the product’s core value can sensibly work in a browser. Browser-specific capability limits are acceptable when they are explicit and the useful core product remains intact; a single desktop-only feature is not by itself a reason to omit an otherwise useful web app.

Web exemption is permitted only when the product’s core function requires infrastructure, privileged device access or hosted compute that CAKE does not currently provide. Each exemption MUST state the blocking capability/infrastructure. Exemptions MUST be re-evaluated when that blocker is removed; exemption is not a permanent product classification.
Mini Computer — a useful web version would require hosted virtualisation/server compute that CAKE does not currently have capacity to provide.

Mini Computer may gain a hosted web mode in the future as a 9to1 subscription capability if sufficient server compute is available. The same principle applies to future apps whose meaningful web implementation requires paid hosted compute.

Windows, 9to1-OS and browser/web MUST implement the useful core authoring and reader experiences for this tranche using the same canonical formats, account identity, domain APIs and permissions. Native interfaces use CUI/Home; web uses the existing authenticated web-service contract and MUST not require arbitrary local filesystem/process access. A narrow viewport by itself is not a reason to replace an otherwise supported app with an unrelated simplified data model.

The single trusted installer MUST install Home, all mandatory modules, the selected app and its app-required dependencies. Selecting a second app MUST reuse compatible shared packages. Internal platform package formats may be used; separate user-facing standalone MSIX installers for individual apps are not the distribution model. Native Windows and 9to1-OS use this contract through their supported packaging mechanisms. Browser apps use authenticated shared web services and MUST NOT require a local Home installation.

Library is Home’s cross-app artifact index/browser, not a duplicate Files app and not a separate storage authority. It MUST surface canonical references to authorised artifacts across 9to1 apps, including recent, favourite/pinned, shared, generated/created and app/type-filtered content where applicable.

9-1 Discover is the model browser/discovery surface inside Home. It MUST aggregate model/catalogue information from configured providers rather than depend on one catalogue. Search, filter and comparison MUST support model identity, provider/origin, modality, capabilities, architecture/parameter information when known, context limits, quantisation/format where known, local/cloud status, hardware-fit estimate, install/connection state, entitlement/cost class and privacy/residency information.

The Universal Model Picker is the single shared model/provider selection and routing interface for the 9to1 ecosystem. On Windows/regular 9to1 it is hosted by Home; on 9to1-OS the same canonical state is surfaced by the OS. Apps, Agents and AI surfaces MUST NOT create incompatible private model pickers, provider registries or fallback logic when this shared capability applies.

Home/Dulche MUST support versioned ordered Model Routes shared by regular 9to1 and 9to1-OS. A Model Route is an ordered list of stable configured model identities plus per-entry enabled/disabled state and routing policy. Users can reorder candidates directly in Home, including by drag/reorder UI, without changing the models' canonical identities.

For local candidates the picker may show estimated RAM/VRAM requirement, current availability, loading state and reclaimable resources when known. On 9to1-OS this integrates with the AI-aware resource manager; on other Home platforms it uses the available Dulche/runtime resource information without pretending OS-level reclamation exists where it does not.
Regular 9to1/Home and 9to1-OS use one canonical Dulche model catalogue and versioned routing contract.

Home Core MUST expose the Shared Productivity Engine as a versioned shared platform capability. Apps may link/embed approved shared engine libraries/components as part of their package for rendering performance, but the canonical schema registry, compatibility negotiation and shared service/version authority remain Home-owned. Apps MUST validate compatible engine/schema versions during startup.

Home MUST support notification history, read/unread state, dismiss/clear subject to retention policy, per-source/category preferences and deep-link actions. Where Windows/9to1-OS system notifications are available, Home MAY bridge eligible notifications to the OS while retaining the canonical 9to1 notification record/state.

directPlatformClauses.text: 9to1 Browse is a full Firefox-derived browser product with native CUI chrome and native CUI internal surfaces. Firefox/Gecko is the primary donor, default web engine and behavioural baseline. Chromium/Blink is a first-class secondary browser/rendering backend available per tab. Browse MUST remain one coherent browser with one canonical 9to1-owned tab/session model; Chromium support MUST NOT be implemented as a second browser bolted onto Firefox or as a separate user profile universe.
Tabs and windows, including restore/reopen behaviour, pinned tabs and normal navigation history.
Web engine architecture

Each web BrowserTab selects a WebEngine value of Firefox/Gecko or Chromium/Blink. The normal user-facing choice SHOULD be labelled Firefox and Chromium; implementation and diagnostics MAY additionally expose the underlying Gecko and Blink engine names. Gecko is the default unless the user or a persisted site rule selects Chromium.

Browse MUST own canonical higher-level browser entities instead of allowing Gecko and Chromium to directly share raw profile databases. At minimum the architecture must model BrowserProfile, BrowserTab, NavigationEntry, Bookmark, HistoryEntry, Download, SitePermission, Workspace, TabGroup, SplitView, SearchProvider, SiteEnhancer and EnginePreference as typed 9to1-owned entities or equivalent strongly typed contracts.

Users MUST be able to use Firefox for this tab, Chromium for this tab, always Firefox for a site/domain, always Chromium for a site/domain, and reset a persisted site engine preference. A broken page SHOULD be switchable to the other engine with one obvious action without opening a separate browser product.

Automatic update does not mean blindly shipping an unvalidated upstream binary. The update pipeline MUST fetch/rebase or reapply maintained 9to1 changes, build the affected engine integration, run Browse compatibility and regression suites, verify CUI integration, engine switching, extension baselines, session/profile isolation, Site Enhancer behaviour, DevTools integration and Dulche browser capabilities, and promote the new engine only after the applicable acceptance gates pass. Security-sensitive upstream releases receive expedited priority. The previous known-good engine build MUST remain rollback-capable until promotion is proven stable.

9to1:// — native 9to1 application surfaces hosted inside a Browse tab, for example 9to1://Spaces, 9to1://Write or a typed deep link such as 9to1://Write/<resource>. These are the actual application surfaces, not web versions or reduced browser copies.
https:// and http:// — ordinary web content. User-facing normal web navigation uses these web schemes; Browse-owned, CUI and native-app content MUST NOT masquerade as an HTTP(S) origin.

Opening 9to1://<App> MUST instantiate the real CUI application surface and the real application services inside the Browse tab. It MUST NOT load a separately implemented web edition, feature-reduced embedded edition or imitation of the app. Responsive layout adaptation is allowed and expected; capability divergence merely because the app is hosted in Browse is not.

9to1 native app tabs participate in normal Browse capabilities including tab groups, pinning, workspaces, restore/reopen and Split View. A user can therefore place 9to1://Write with a research document beside an https:// research page, or combine two different native 9to1 apps, without requiring a separate web version of either app.

Browser profiles are tab-scoped, not window-scoped. Every BrowserTab carries a ProfileID or equivalent profile context, allowing one window, one workspace and one Split View to contain tabs from different profiles simultaneously.

A BrowserProfile is an identity/storage/privacy boundary. Depending on supported configuration, it owns or scopes cookies, login sessions, site storage, site permissions, browsing-data attribution, extensions and extension state, search preferences, Site Enhancers, credentials/passkeys and other profile-specific browser configuration.

Profile identity MUST be visually discoverable on tabs and in relevant browser UI so the user can tell which account/session context will be used. Consequential actions and Dulche-controlled actions SHOULD make the active profile context clear where confusion could cause the action to occur under the wrong identity.

Changing a tab to another profile MUST reopen/recreate its web session under the destination profile rather than copying authentication material across profile boundaries. Safe navigation/organisation metadata such as URL, group, workspace and split position may be preserved where applicable.

Browse MUST provide modern tab management in addition to Firefox donor parity. Tab groups are first-class canonical entities with stable identity, naming, optional colour/icon metadata, collapse/expand state, persistence, restore, drag/drop and movement between windows/workspaces. Dulche and other typed APIs can address a group directly.

Split View displays two independent BrowserTab entities side-by-side in one browser content area with a resizable divider. The split container owns presentation only; each pane remains a real tab with its own URL/route, navigation history, profile, renderer/backend where applicable and canonical tab identity.

A split may mix any compatible tab surface classes, including web + web, 9to1 app + web, 9to1 app + 9to1 app, Browse internal + web and tabs from different BrowserProfiles. Either pane can be swapped, unsplit or moved without destroying the underlying tab.

The canvas can host deterministic widgets, browser widgets, 9to1 app widgets, extension-provided CUI widgets, static content and Generative Areas. It SHOULD reuse shared 9to1 canvas/layout infrastructure where practical instead of creating an incompatible bespoke layout system.

Search mode performs normal navigation/search behaviour and MUST NOT invoke an LLM merely to execute an ordinary URL or provider query. AI mode sends the request to Dulche and can use permissioned Browse capabilities and referenced browser/app context.
Dulche browser experience

Dulche is the only authoritative AI system in Browse. Firefox-provided proprietary AI surfaces MUST be removed/replaced. Browse SHOULD provide both a persistent Dulche sidebar for larger tasks and a lightweight floating/command bar for contextual requests, using the shared Dulche runtime rather than launching a browser-specific model server.

The Dulche UI MUST support @-mentioning canonical browser context. At minimum users can mention tabs and SHOULD be able to mention tab groups, workspaces, split panes and other supported Browse entities. Mention autocomplete resolves to stable canonical IDs rather than copying only titles/URLs into the prompt.

Permission scope MUST be explicit and composable. The implementation must support equivalents of read this page, control this tab, control these selected tabs and control Browse for this task. Granting one scope MUST NOT silently grant permanent global browser control.

Browser automation SHOULD use structured semantic capabilities such as Navigate, OpenTab, CloseTab, ActivateTab, ReadPage, ReadElement, Find, Scroll, Click, FillField, SelectOption, GoBack, GoForward and Reload when structured control exists. Blind coordinate input is a fallback, not the primary architecture.

Split panes and tabs SHOULD support semantic drag/drop. Where both surfaces understand a canonical 9to1 entity, transfer the typed entity/link instead of degrading it to copied text. Examples include dragging a Maps place into Planner or a Board item into Write. Web upload targets may receive files through normal browser security/permission rules.

cui://, browse:// and 9to1:// are privileged/non-web namespaces with separate routing and origin/capability rules. Ordinary HTTP(S) pages MUST NOT be able to inspect native app state, call privileged CUI/Browse APIs, forge trusted 9to1:// content or inherit internal permissions simply by navigating to or linking an internal route.

A web page may request navigation to an allowed registered internal route only through the normal navigation/policy boundary. Navigating to 9to1:// does not grant the originating site the destination app's authority. Profile cookies/credentials and engine-private state MUST remain isolated according to their owning profile/backend.

Browse MUST handle Firefox renderer crashes, Chromium renderer crashes, whole-browser crashes, failed engine startup, unavailable selected engines, extension incompatibility, interrupted downloads, invalid/corrupt engine-private state and failed engine switches without corrupting the other engine or canonical Browse profile state.
Dulche @ mentions resolve to canonical browser/app entities and permissioned autonomous browsing uses semantic browser capabilities with consequential-action safeguards.

Cakemods.com MUST host a web version of every 9-1 Workspace/AI product that is not explicitly listed as web-exempt. Web surfaces MUST share the same CAKE ID identity, canonical artifact formats, domain APIs, permission model and underlying server-side entities as desktop equivalents. Browser-specific UI/layout MAY differ, but it MUST NOT create a separate incompatible product model.

The default rule is to provide a web version whenever the product’s core value can sensibly work in a browser. Browser-specific capability limits are acceptable when they are explicit and the useful core product remains intact; a single desktop-only feature is not by itself a reason to omit an otherwise useful web app.

Web exemption is permitted only when the product’s core function requires infrastructure, privileged device access or hosted compute that CAKE does not currently provide. Each exemption MUST state the blocking capability/infrastructure. Exemptions MUST be re-evaluated when that blocker is removed; exemption is not a permanent product classification.
Mini Computer — a useful web version would require hosted virtualisation/server compute that CAKE does not currently have capacity to provide.

Mini Computer may gain a hosted web mode in the future as a 9to1 subscription capability if sufficient server compute is available. The same principle applies to future apps whose meaningful web implementation requires paid hosted compute.

9to1 web apps authenticate against CAKEMODS/CAKE ID using a browser-based OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow with PKCE or an equivalent secure public-client flow. Desktop, web and open-source/custom clients are treated as untrusted public clients: they receive short-lived user access tokens and never contain provider keys, billing secrets or entitlement-signing secrets.

Authentication/session operations must support account sign-in/sign-out, current-user/profile lookup, active-session/device inspection and revocation. Sensitive account or billing changes use trusted CAKEMODS web flows rather than accepting raw payment credentials through the open-source client.
Web subscription behaviour

Web and desktop clients MUST resolve account state from the same CAKE ID and entitlement service. For the same account and organisation context, plan identity, Dust balance, hosted-storage usage, site quota/usage and applicable feature entitlements MUST be consistent across official clients, subject only to explicitly documented platform capability differences.

Where a future web feature requires material hosted compute that is not available on the free/local product - for example hosted Mini Computer virtual machines - it may be offered as a subscription-backed server capability with explicit resource limits. The browser UI must never pretend that local-only or unavailable server compute exists.

Business is an organisation collaboration and management capability set, not merely labels on pricing cards. It comprises Team Space and an organisation drive; organisation Connect; cross-account device Mesh; pooled or individually partitioned usage; team-wide Agents; and device-level policy controls for managed 9to1-OS Business accounts. 9to1 Admin supplies their management interface, while the existing apps retain canonical ownership of their domain data.

Mesh MUST expose availability, queued/running jobs, utilisation, failure and cancellation/revocation outcomes. Revocation blocks new work and cancels or safely terminates existing work where supported; it must not claim to undo already completed actions or erase copies outside its actual control. A disconnected device remains unavailable/pending, never fictitiously running a workload. Windows and 9to1-OS expose only supported native capabilities; web can manage grants and observe jobs without pretending to supply privileged local resources.
BIZ-07 — Managed 9to1-OS accounts and device policy

Business MUST provide device-level administrative controls for explicitly enrolled managed 9to1-OS Business accounts. Controls MUST cover supported app/package and Plugin installation/enablement restrictions, allowed features and Automations, required organisation/role Plugins, enforced settings, default-model/routing policy and Mesh-resource participation. Existing compatibility-framework and privileged-operation restrictions continue to apply beneath every launch surface.

Managed account policy is not automatic whole-device ownership. Personal users, personal artifacts and unenrolled devices remain outside the organisation’s authority. Destructive remote actions, full-device wipe, arbitrary privileged shell access and surveillance are not implicitly authorised by Business. Other operating systems may expose supported Mesh and app policy, but they must not claim complete 9to1-OS endpoint-management parity without an explicit capability implementation.

Home installation includes the Home Core background service/runtime required by native apps plus the Home user-facing CUI shell. Native apps require a compatible Home installation/Home Core service, but the visible Home window does not need to remain open while other apps run. On 9to1-OS, Home Core may be integrated as a system component while preserving the same service contracts.

Library is Home’s cross-app artifact index/browser, not a duplicate Files app and not a separate storage authority. It MUST surface canonical references to authorised artifacts across 9to1 apps, including recent, favourite/pinned, shared, generated/created and app/type-filtered content where applicable.

9-1 Discover is the model browser/discovery surface inside Home. It MUST aggregate model/catalogue information from configured providers rather than depend on one catalogue. Search, filter and comparison MUST support model identity, provider/origin, modality, capabilities, architecture/parameter information when known, context limits, quantisation/format where known, local/cloud status, hardware-fit estimate, install/connection state, entitlement/cost class and privacy/residency information.

The Universal Model Picker is the single shared model/provider selection and routing interface for the 9to1 ecosystem. On Windows/regular 9to1 it is hosted by Home; on 9to1-OS the same canonical state is surfaced by the OS. Apps, Agents and AI surfaces MUST NOT create incompatible private model pickers, provider registries or fallback logic when this shared capability applies.

Home/Dulche MUST support versioned ordered Model Routes shared by regular 9to1 and 9to1-OS. A Model Route is an ordered list of stable configured model identities plus per-entry enabled/disabled state and routing policy. Users can reorder candidates directly in Home, including by drag/reorder UI, without changing the models' canonical identities.

For local candidates the picker may show estimated RAM/VRAM requirement, current availability, loading state and reclaimable resources when known. On 9to1-OS this integrates with the AI-aware resource manager; on other Home platforms it uses the available Dulche/runtime resource information without pretending OS-level reclamation exists where it does not.
Regular 9to1/Home and 9to1-OS use one canonical Dulche model catalogue and versioned routing contract.

Home Core MUST expose the Shared Productivity Engine as a versioned shared platform capability. Apps may link/embed approved shared engine libraries/components as part of their package for rendering performance, but the canonical schema registry, compatibility negotiation and shared service/version authority remain Home-owned. Apps MUST validate compatible engine/schema versions during startup.

Home MUST support notification history, read/unread state, dismiss/clear subject to retention policy, per-source/category preferences and deep-link actions. Where Windows/9to1-OS system notifications are available, Home MAY bridge eligible notifications to the OS while retaining the canonical 9to1 notification record/state.
Windows: Home provides the full native hub/shell, Home Core background services and the Home-hosted Universal Model Picker. Native apps depend on the compatible Home installation/Home Core handshake.

The Universal Model Picker is OS-hosted while using the same canonical Dulche/model/provider state. 9to1-OS MUST NOT create divergent duplicate settings/package/model databases.

It MUST capability-negotiate and clearly mark local-only/native-only functions such as local package management, local models/devices or unavailable Home Core services rather than pretending they exist in-browser.

The web app uses authenticated shared web services without requiring a local Home installation for ordinary organisation administration. Device operations require an enrolled compatible endpoint; a browser cannot directly enforce unsupported local OS controls. Unsupported capabilities MUST remain distinguishable from denied permission or an offline device.

Admin owns management workflows and policy editing. The account/billing service owns subscriptions and ledgers; Spaces owns Team Spaces; Files owns shared-drive content; Connect owns communications; Home/Mesh owns pairing and device-resource execution; Dulche/Den owns Agents; the 9to1-OS policy service owns endpoint enforcement. Admin MUST invoke these canonical services rather than create duplicate content, Agent registries, payment records or a competing permission broker. Controls MUST include organisation, role and member ceilings for AI usage and applicable storage/site resources; warnings and hard-stop behaviour; configured time windows; and model/Agent/Automation attribution. A hard ceiling is enforced before work is admitted. No paid overage or automatic top-up is enabled merely because a warning threshold is crossed. Reports MUST separate allocated, available, reserved, consumed, rolled-over and expired credits and display the reset/expiry policy and freshness.

It MUST be available to supported editable text surfaces such as Write, Spaces, Mail, Boards, Present speaker notes, Planner descriptions, Sites, AI Studio and other CUI text editors through the shared platform capability.

Native Windows/9to1-OS may provide the full OS-global Overlay, native window/display capture and background voice capabilities. Web may provide microphone, camera and browser-authorised screen sharing but MUST NOT claim an OS-global Overlay outside the browser. Mobile uses supported camera/microphone/share-sheet/screen-capture capabilities. All surfaces capability-negotiate rather than assuming parity.
Web/native capability differences are reported accurately, including no false claim of OS-global Overlay on web.

Plugins / Connectors lists canonical Dulche Plugins, MCP/external connectors and applicable 9to1 app capability bindings available to the Agent. + Add opens the relevant Dulche capability browser. A GameDefinition MUST declare the game-specific capability profile available to Agent contestants. Tools such as web search, calculators, code execution, Files, Plugins or external connectors may be Allowed, Denied or constrained per game/role.

Disallowed capabilities MUST be removed/blocked at runtime rather than merely discouraged in instructions. A no-calculator maths quiz cannot expose calculator/code/web tools to Agent contestants. A research contest may explicitly permit them.
Game-specific tool restrictions are enforced at runtime, including a no-web/no-code/no-calculator quiz profile.

It MUST behave like a mature word processor rather than a web editor, site builder, Markdown editor, collection of HTML blocks or browser contenteditable surface. LibreOffice Writer/LibreOfficeKit is the mature donor/layout/format engine for text-oriented documents; 9to1 owns the CUI shell, shared Productivity Engine integration, collaboration, AI, Sections model and native extensions.

The Write shell remains consistent while an appropriate PDF/page-object engine (including applicable LibreOffice Draw/PDF capabilities or equivalent mature implementation) owns fixed-layout PDF object semantics.
Write uses a real structured word-processing/document engine and is not implemented as a generic HTML/contenteditable/web editor.
A platform capability is supported only when the platform capability registry declares the required capability and version for the active device/runtime.

REPLACE_WITH_9TO1_NATIVE_EQUIVALENT is used when 9to1 already owns the equivalent platform capability, including CUI shell/UI, Dulche AI, Home permission handling, Files storage integration or other shared 9to1 services.
Supported platforms and capability negotiation

Canvas MUST ship on every 9to1 platform for which the app is not explicitly exempt under the global platform/web rules. Desktop/native and web implementations MUST share the same Canvas artifact schema, stable identities, domain API semantics and server-side canonical entities.
Platform-specific input or rendering capability differences MUST be negotiated explicitly. Hardware capability absence MUST NOT be misrepresented as format incapability.
Native and web/open-on-lower-capability round trips preserve unsupported pressure/tilt and other stored data.

Scoped Chat is a closed-corpus notebook-style Chat PageType. Its answers MUST be grounded only in the authorised contents of the containing Board plus the explicit source collection attached to that Scoped Chat. It MUST NOT search the public web, invoke external-information retrieval tools or consult unrelated connected-app content to fill evidence gaps.
Platform capability behaviour

Boards MUST ship useful supported native behaviour on Windows and 9to1-OS and a useful web version under the global web-product contract. All clients operate on the same Board/Page/artifact identities and canonical revisions. Platform capability differences MUST be explicit and queryable rather than silently dropping features.

Browser/native differences may include pen pressure/tilt, OS file drag-and-drop, clipboard richness, filesystem access, windowing and availability of specialised embedded surfaces. When a capability is unavailable, Boards MUST provide the closest useful supported interaction or a clear unsupported-capability state without corrupting or flattening the underlying artifact.
Windows, 9to1-OS and web clients capability-negotiate declared differences while preserving the same canonical Board/Page/artifact identities.
Platform capability behaviour

Planner MUST provide useful supported native behaviour on Windows and 9to1-OS plus a useful web version under the global web contract. All clients operate on the same canonical Planner/provider entities.

Native clients MAY have richer OS notification/calendar integration; web may depend on browser notification/background constraints. Capability differences are explicit and MUST NOT silently downgrade the canonical planning state or turn the web app into a read-only viewer.
Windows, 9to1-OS and web preserve the same canonical entity model while surfacing declared capability differences.
Platform capability behaviour

Picture MUST provide useful Windows, 9to1-OS and web editing/creation experiences over the same PictureDocument model. Codec, RAW, HDR, GPU effect, pen/tilt and local/remote AI capability differences are explicit and queryable.

The web app MUST NOT degrade into a read-only image viewer. Unsupported platform features are disabled with a capability reason while preserving the canonical document so another capable client can continue editing.
Windows, 9to1-OS and web preserve the same canonical document model while capability-negotiating codecs/GPU/AI/pen differences.
Platform capability behaviour

Wave MUST provide useful Windows, 9to1-OS and web editing/creation experiences over the same canonical project model. Input devices, realtime audio APIs, codecs, plugin/instrument backends, MIDI/controller access and local/cloud model capabilities are explicit/queryable.

Web MUST remain a useful multitrack/sequencer/editor experience rather than a static player. Unsupported platform capabilities are disabled with a clear reason while preserving project state for another capable client.
Windows, 9to1-OS and web preserve the same project/generated-component model while capability-negotiating audio hardware/backend differences.
Platform capability behaviour

Windows, 9to1-OS and web preserve the same canonical Motion project/graph/generated-component model while capability-negotiating codecs, GPU/hardware acceleration, camera/device access, model availability and performance differences.
Windows, 9to1-OS and web preserve the same canonical project model while capability-negotiating backend/hardware/model differences.

Data MUST provide native SQL authoring/execution with syntax highlighting, dialect-aware parsing/validation, schema/object browser, table/column/function completion, relationship-aware join suggestions, query formatting, parameters where supported, saved queries, query history, execution timing/statistics, cancellation, paged/virtualised result sets, EXPLAIN/plan access where supported and result export/materialisation.
Platform capability behaviour

Windows, 9to1-OS and web preserve the same canonical Data project/workbook/schema/query/pipeline/cube/Visualisation model while capability-negotiating local DuckDB execution, LibreOffice-derived compatibility components, external database drivers, file access and hardware/resource differences.
Windows, 9to1-OS and web preserve the same canonical Data model while capability-negotiating local/provider execution differences.

Authors can configure logos, organisation branding, custom header/footer, background artwork and hosted-form identity. Custom domains/advanced branding integrate with the wider 9to1 web platform where supported.

Forms MUST provide configurable anti-cheat/integrity controls, with stronger options available for Tests and live assessments while making clear that browser-based controls reduce opportunities but cannot guarantee that cheating is impossible.
Platform capability behaviour

Windows, 9to1-OS and web preserve the same canonical FormProject, response, mode, Data binding, graph and multiplayer-session model while capability-negotiating device features, realtime transport, identity providers, proctoring/kiosk integrations and mathematical/rendering backends.
A standard live multiplayer quiz synchronises question state, answer windows, scoring and reveal using server-authoritative state.
Windows, 9to1-OS and web preserve the same canonical Forms model while capability-negotiating platform-specific realtime/integrity features.

First-party examples include console applications, CUI applications, class/static/shared libraries, web/API services, test projects, Python packages/CLI applications, Sites projects, Android/mobile projects, operating-system/kernel/bootloader projects, 9to1 extensions, CUI component libraries, AI provider/tool projects and other supported templates.

Examples include console → terminal, web → development server + preview, Android → emulator/device install + launch, CUI application → application runtime, 9to1 extension → extension development host, operating system → virtual machine, and library → test/sample host where configured.

Extensions MAY contribute language/toolchain/debugger/formatter/linter providers, project templates, package providers, editors, commands, tool windows, CUI/visual-builder components, AI context/tools, Node Graph node types and product-specific contributions exposed by host APIs.

Extensions use a versioned manifest declaring ExtensionID, publisher/name/version, compatible host/API versions, entry points, target products, contributions, permissions/capabilities, dependencies, supported platforms, assets, update channel and signature/provenance.

Web/Sites-compatible Run/Preview may use Sites preview/runtime infrastructure for responsive preview, route inspection, development server integration, preview environments and deployment-oriented diagnostics without Dev duplicating the entire Sites authoring product.

Applicable previews are interactive. CUI/web previews can accept pointer/keyboard/navigation input, resize, hover/focus state and other runtime interactions without becoming the general Browse product.
Platform capability behaviour

Windows, 9to1-OS and web preserve the same canonical Dev project/workspace/action models while capability-negotiating local compiler availability, process execution, VM acceleration, terminal/debugger integration, filesystem access, extension hosting and remote environments.
Windows, 9to1-OS and web preserve the same canonical Dev model while capability-negotiating unsupported local execution features.
